The key structural gap is NL-CONTRACT-NL2-ENDPOINT-2: NL requires BrakingState -> OperationalState on 'signal transmission fails', but the complete transition inventory has no such edge; the existing Signal_Transmission_Fails edge is InitialState -> OperationalState (tr_0003), a different source. The guard-disjointness contracts (NL2-GUARDDISJ-1, NL3-DERIVED) are non-executable multi-alternative distinguishability claims better suited to the behavior_consequence lens's predicate-null W1 treatment, but since this lens also must address structural contrast of the transition group, I include one derived observation: the group's alternatives project onto exact distinct triggers (Signal_Feedback_Sent vs the nonexistent failure edge), so the primary defect is the missing edge itself, not guard collision, which I leave to the other lens/unresolved as appropriate. issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue NL2's overall paragraph describes a single sequential flow (initial->braking; then transmission-fails->operational; then feedback-sent->initial) all rooted at the initial state, so the 'signal transmission fails' branch may have been authored as an alternative first-entry outcome from InitialState rather than from BrakingState, meaning the intended source could be InitialState (already satisfied by tr_0003). However, the contract's own binding hints explicitly fix source=braking state, and the NL sentence sequence ('When ... transitions ... to the braking state. If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state.') most naturally reads as a continuation from the just-entered braking state, so the missing braking-state-sourced edge remains the exact obligation to evaluate under this contract's stated source.

issues.observed: The closed FCSTM shows BrakingState has exactly two outgoing transitions: transition:line:15 (BrakingState->ClampingState, trigger=Entering_Clamping_State, guard=null) and transition:line:17 (BrakingState->InitialState, trigger=Signal_Feedback_Sent, guard=null). Neither carries a guard field; the NL2 'signal transmission fails' alternative is not even realized as an outgoing edge from BrakingState in the closed model (that condition only appears on InitialState->OperationalState, transition:line:14). No guard predicate exists to formally establish the required disjointness/exclusivity contemplated by the contract for BrakingState's alternatives.
issues.reason: guard_disjointness is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate per instructions since the registry has no frozen predicate expressing cross-alternative guard/trigger distinguishability; the exact guard fields on both real outgoing transitions from BrakingState are null, which is the precise negative fact under review for this contract.
issues.requirement_quote: If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state. Once the signal feedback is sent, it returns to the initial state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The two BrakingState outgoing transitions (line:15 and line:17) already carry distinct triggers (Entering_Clamping_State vs Signal_Feedback_Sent), so event-based selection may be considered sufficient real-world disjointness even without an explicit guard field, since pyfcstm dispatches transitions by triggering event rather than requiring guards when only one transition per event exists from a state.
issues.title: BrakingState outgoing alternatives to OperationalState-guard-failure path and InitialState-feedback path are not distinguished by any formal guard in the closed model
